details.abstract: Long-form multi-shot video editing requires an intended edit to remain coherent across abrupt changes in scene, viewpoint, and subject appearance, while processing substantially longer visual context than conventional single-shot editors. We introduce MoviEdit , an end-to-end framework for scalable long-form multi-shot video editing that jointly addresses the challenges of (1) data , (2) modeling , and (3) evaluation . Project page: https://multi-shot-edit.github.io/

title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling

details.title: Behind Video Generation: Observations and Insights on Multimodal Understanding from Kling
details.abstract: This technical report shares practical lessons from the evolution of Kling’s video-generation systems. It argues that the next bottleneck is no longer visual rendering, but semantic control—the ability to understand what to generate, preserve, organize, and evaluate. Centered on Kling-MLLM, the report examines the full data–conditioning–alignment–evaluation pipeline, covering dense and reference-grounded captioning, prompt enhancement, perceptually grounded text encoders, reward models, and task-specific evaluation. It offers a valuable system-level perspective on how multimodal understanding enables more controllable, coherent, and production-ready video generation.

title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner

details.title: DreamX: Video Diffusion Model is a Universal Latent Action Learner
details.abstract: DreamX turns a pretrained video diffusion model into a latent action learner. Its encoder reads compact latent actions out of human and robot videos while the video prior takes care of appearance, so the latents capture motion alone. The same latent actions then drive video transfer, human-to-robot action transfer, and a compact latent policy. Project Page: https://cvlab-kaist.github.io/DreamX/

title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified

details.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
details.abstract: Introducing Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified. Strong scientific reasoning and tool use with a simple post-training recipe: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning. Learn to reason: model-aware construction of challenging, self-contained scientific problems. Learn to investigate: verifiable tasks that require retrieving information and using tools. Learn through interaction: reinforcement learning over agent trajectories. With approximately 18K SFT examples, Axion 1.0-35B and 122B achieve competitive results across six evaluation settings: HLE, BioMysteryBench, SEAL-0, HiPhO, and the Olympiad and Research splits of FrontierScience. The Axion 1.0-35B reproduction checkpoint is now available under Apache 2.0. It scores 52.8 on HLE, 35.3 on BioMysteryBench, 60.4 on SEAL-0, 45.9 on HiPhO, 85.0 on FrontierScience Olympiad, and 55.0 on FrontierScience Research. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03233 Project: https://axion1-0.github.io/ Code: https://github.com/bytedance/axion1_0 Training data: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Axion1-0/axion-training-data Model (35B reproduction): https://huggingface.co/Axion1-0/Axion-1.0-35B

title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild

details.title: RoboColosseum: Evaluating Physical Intelligence at Scale In-The-Wild
details.abstract: General-purpose robot policies must work across robots, tasks, and environments, yet the variation that makes physical trials informative also makes them difficult to reproduce. We introduce RoboColosseum, a distributed evaluation framework that combines unified policy serving and standardized protocols across a network of locally operated robots in diverse environments. Our initial study evaluates five vision-language-action (VLA) policies and three frontier AI agents across four embodiments (SO-101, Franka, Bimanual-YAM, and G1 Humanoid). The Open Track compares models without task-specific adaptation in blinded, pairwise trials under matched local conditions. The Fine-tune Track measures how well VLA policies adapt to 20 tasks when each policy receives the same 100 demonstrations per task. Across 5,699 Open Track comparisons at 124 sites, frontier agents rival specialized VLA policies, though all systems struggle to complete open-world tasks reliably. After fine-tuning, GR00T N1.7 leads on SO-101 and π0.5 leads on Franka and Bimanual-YAM. Policy rankings show weak agreement across embodiment-specific task suites (Kendall’s W = 0.24). Open Track rankings poorly predict relative performance after fine-tuning, with substantial rank reversals on all three embodiments shared between tracks. Measuring partial progress reveals differences that task success alone misses. On the G1 Humanoid, no policy completes any of the five tasks, yet average progress ranges from 13.3% to 23.2% across policies. Open Track rankings stabilize as trials accumulate, and active matchmaking achieves comparable ranking agreement with substantially fewer physical trials than uniform sampling. These results show how distributed physical evaluation can reveal where robot policies generalize, how well they adapt to new tasks, and how far they progress on tasks they fail to complete.

title: Factorized MLLM Embeddings for Composed Image Retrieval

title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents

details.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
details.abstract: Happy to share our latest work on agent environment synthesis: 🌟 ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents Most existing environment synthesis methods are data-centric: they first build the underlying database, then synthesize tools and tasks. Tool interfaces easily drift from reality, and it is hard to form tasks that span environments. ToolSpace takes the opposite approach. It first collects tools from real call traces, then chains real tool sets into a tool universe, and finally synthesizes the underlying database on demand. This preserves authenticity while flexibly generating verifiable tasks across any environment × any tool. 💡 Key methods 1️⃣ Tool universe exploration: mine tool dependencies from real traces and link them into a tool-world graph; synthesize databases only for environments that change state. 2️⃣ Verifiable task synthesis: walk the graph with state-aware traversal and backtracking, decompile executable tool chains into tasks and verification scripts, and keep environment state continuous. The same chain can yield high-quality SFT data and mixed-environment RL data. 3️⃣ Harder evaluation benchmarks: ToolSpace seamlessly upgrades two frontier benchmarks into AutomationBench Pro and τ³-Bench Banking Pro. Strong existing models all score below 40, setting a harder bar for the field. 📊 Experiments ✅ We evaluate ToolSpace-8B, 35B, and 744B on 7 long-horizon tool benchmarks. ToolSpace-744B averages 56.6, on par with Claude Opus 5. ✅ ToolSpace-744B: AutomationBench 54.7, Harvey LAB 27.5, SkillsBench 67.8, OfficeQA Pro 67.1, JobBench 57.5. ✅ Agent performance scales as environment and data scale grow. We welcome discussion and feedback. Code and models are open-sourced 👏👏👏 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.05036 🌐 Project page: https://toolspace-agent.github.io/ 💻 GitHub: https://github.com/dongguanting/ToolSpace 🤗 Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/collections/dongguanting/toolspace

title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams

details.title: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
details.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on collaboration among specialized agents to solve complex tasks. Existing methods improve MAS by refining the prompts, skills, and execution strategies of individual agents based on task feedback. However, improving individual agents does not necessarily lead to better team collaboration. Recent studies have therefore extended evolution to the collaboration level, using collective execution experience to adjust team organization, and inter-agent interactions. Nevertheless, evolving collaboration across heterogeneous tasks remains challenging, as existing approaches often constrain team reorganization within a shared structure and reuse interaction rules across incompatible team contexts. In this paper, we propose EvoTeam, a collaboration-centric evolution framework that jointly evolves team organization, interaction rules, and individual agent skills through execution experience. It maintains a library of reusable teams, selecting or creating agent teams and guiding collaboration through team-specific interaction rules. Collaboration experience accumulates within compatible team contexts, while individual skills remain reusable across teams. Experiments across four benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness. Our code is available at https://github.com/DEEP-JLU/EvoTeam .

title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks

details.title: VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks
details.abstract: 🚀 We are excited to share our latest work: “VidUEU-Agent: A Data-Curation Agent for Multimodal Understanding, Editing, and Unified Tasks”! The scarcity and high annotation cost of high-quality multimodal instruction data remain major bottlenecks for multimodal model development. Raw videos contain rich visual knowledge and temporal information, but transforming them into accurate, verifiable, and task-oriented instruction data remains challenging. To address this, we introduce VidUEU-Agent, an agentic data-curation framework that automatically constructs instruction data from raw videos for multimodal understanding, image editing, and unified understanding-and-generation tasks. 🔑 Key Highlights 🎬 Four-Stage Data Construction Pipeline: VidUEU-Agent performs global perception to analyze video structure and filter low-quality shots, mines informative keyframes and multimodal signals, constructs structured metadata, and routes each metadata entry to suitable task types for instruction synthesis. Agent planning, tool use, and multi-stage quality control support the entire process. 🔍 Evidence-Grounded Data Synthesis: The framework combines vision-language models with visual tools for quality assessment, semantic analysis, and information verification. During instruction synthesis, the model cites the evidence signals it uses, improving data traceability and factual consistency. 🔄 Autonomous Iteration with Training Feedback: VidUEU-Agent uses downstream training and evaluation results to identify weaknesses and refine data distributions across capabilities, domains, and task types. Across four iterations, each using 30K samples to fine-tune BAGEL from the same initial checkpoint, performance improves overall on the three feedback benchmarks: 📦 VidUEU-100K Dataset: Using this pipeline, we construct VidUEU-100K from 8,268 diverse videos, containing nearly 20,000 dense metadata annotations and 100,000 instruction samples: 40K understanding, 30K editing, and 30K unified samples, spanning nine task paradigms and five scenario categories. Our work demonstrates how raw videos can be transformed into diverse, evidence-grounded instruction data through agent planning, tool augmentation, and training-feedback-driven refinement. We hope VidUEU-Agent and VidUEU-100K provide a scalable and reproducible foundation for developing unified multimodal models. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04418 💻 Code: https://github.com/LRuca/VidUEU-Agent 🤗 Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lruca/VidUEU100k We welcome feedback and discussions!

title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments

details.title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
details.abstract: We introduce WebHarbor, a suite of 153 executable, dockerized website environments that reconstruct the visual interfaces, content, and workflows of real-world web services, plus 3,518 tasks for evaluating and training GUI web agents. Why: live-web evaluation is unstable. In our runs, about 38% of Online-Mind2Web tasks were blocked by bot detection, and 22% of WebVoyager tasks were outdated. Core contributions: Environments: task-driven human-agent collaboration. Coding agents implement each site, and human reviewers audit visual fidelity, functional correctness, and task validity. 57 contributors from 26 affiliations built the suite in five months. Each environment averages 37.3 pages and 1,319.9 images, the most of any compared suite. Tasks: multi-step and post-authentication workflows (accounts, bookings, transactions) that live-web benchmarks largely lack, graded by verifiers that check the final answer and the state changes, with fast resets for RL. Results: trained with RL only in WebHarbor, WebHarbor-4B reaches a 75.8 average on WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web, 5.2 points above the live-web-trained OpenWebRL-4B and 22.2 above the shared SFT checkpoint. All 15 WebVoyager websites are excluded from training. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03634 Project page: https://aiming-lab.github.io/WebHarbor/ Code: https://github.com/aiming-lab/WebHarbor Environments: https://huggingface.co/datasets/ChilleD/WebHarbor Tasks (Harbor format): https://huggingface.co/datasets/ChilleD/WebHarbor-Tasks Model: https://huggingface.co/ChilleD/WebHarbor-4B Docker images: https://hub.docker.com/r/wildawm/webharbor

title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents

details.title: "Shall We Approve?" Consequence-Aware Approval for Autonomous Coding Agents
details.abstract: Does a coding agent really know what its next command will do? Approving every command by hand does not scale: Claude Code users approve 93% of permission prompts anyway. So agents now rely on automated approvers, such as Claude Code's Auto Mode, rule-based checkers, and guardrail models. All of them judge the text of the command. Yet a command's behavior is decided by the scripts it invokes and the workspace it runs in, and the same command can be harmless in one project and destructive in another. We propose Caper , which approves a command after seeing what it does. Each command is pre-executed in a snapshotted sandbox under system-call tracing. An LLM approver reviews a compact report of the observed effects: file changes, network attempts, and reads of secrets. Allowed commands are committed; blocked ones are rolled back, and the agent gets a reason it can act on. Compared with six existing systems, Caper has the lowest harmful-outcome rate on SABER (6.7% vs. at least 14.8%) and on YoloFS-Ext, our benchmark that hides harm inside the tools agents are asked to run (7.8% vs. at least 35.3%). It blocks only 1.0% of the safe twins. Code and data: https://github.com/wudaoz/Caper

title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations

details.title: PrimeSim: A Generalist World Model Simulator from Large-Scale Cross-Embodiment Demonstrations
details.abstract: PrimeSim is an action-conditioned, multiview world model that runs as a robot simulator. It starts from a pretrained video generator, midtrains on 30,110 hours across 22 platforms, then posttrains into a causal few-step generator. Posttraining combines self-rollout training, so the model learns from its own generated histories rather than only real frames, with a selected KV-cache memory that carries context across chunks. Inference runs at over 10 FPS with all three camera views. PrimeSim scores first overall on EWMBench and leads four of five WorldSimProbe suites against state-of-the-art baselines. Rollouts stay coherent over long horizons and transfer to held-out platforms within 100-200 gradient steps. We also use the model as an environment for reinforcement learning: GRPO post-training inside PrimeSim raises LIBERO success from 61.7% to 73.2%, and the model's success predictions track the physics simulator closely enough to rank policies. All experiments are in simulation (AgiBot G2, LIBERO, RoboTwin); no physical robot is used, and closed-loop hardware deployment is future work. Weights and code will be released on the 6th of November. Project page: https://primebottech.github.io/PrimeSim-website/

title: Mage-VL-Cowork: A Full Training Recipe to Learn Hybrid Computer Use From Evolved Harnesses

Our 4B model achieves 66.0% on OSWorld-Verified, advancing on-device intelligence. Model is released at https://huggingface.co/microsoft/Mage-VL-Cowork .

title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems

details.title: Recursa: Toward Recursively Self-Improving Foundation Model Systems
details.abstract: When a foundation model moves into a new domain, there's usually little expert-written data or reliable supervision to train on. Recursa adapts to the domain by learning from its own experience, without human experts or a stronger teacher model. A knowledge repository stores what the system learns: domain-specific skills, instructions on when to use them, memories of past tasks, and reflections on what to improve. Bootstrapping: the system builds the repository from domain materials and practices on tasks it generates from them. This targets the knowledge gap. Recursive self-improvement: parallel learners run tasks and propose local improvements, which are validated and merged back into the repository. This targets the behavior gap. The system's own model drives the whole process, including improving how it learns. On Harvey LAB's Firm Knowledge benchmark, Recursa raises the all-pass rate on held-out test tasks from 30.0% to 55.0% with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and from 35.0% to 46.0% with Qwen3.8-Flash. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04035

title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation

details.title: Every Token Needs Its Own Teacher: Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-distillation
details.abstract: On-policy Self-distillation (OPSD) has proven effective for post-training large language models by constructing a teacher conditioned on privileged references. However, existing approaches keep the teacher fixed either throughout training by consistently exposing it to the full reference, or within each response by adaptively varying partial reference exposure only across responses. In this paper, we argue that neither of them is sufficient. Instead, every token needs its own teacher, as the teacher preference can vary token by token within the same response. Through a teacher-intervention pilot study, we validate that the teacher preference differs across tokens, and reveal that a preferred teacher can be identified for each token through majority voting and KL-based selection. Motivated by these findings, we propose Multi-teacher Adaptive On-policy Self-Distillation (MTA-OPSD), the first token-level adaptive OPSD method. Our method constructs a multi-teacher pool consisting of candidate teachers, and enables every token to adaptively select its preferred teacher during training. Experiments with Qwen3 models on mathematical reasoning tasks show that MTA-OPSD consistently outperforms existing OPSD approaches with an average gain of up to +5.9 over the base model, highlighting the importance of adapting teacher supervision at the token level. The code is available at https://github.com/xingzhejun/MTA-OPSD .

title: Switch-SWE: Do Coding Agents Hold Focus When Switching Between Unfinished Tasks?

details.title: Switch-SWE: Do Coding Agents Hold Focus When Switching Between Unfinished Tasks?
details.abstract: Switch-SWE is a repository-level benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can resume a focus task after working on other unfinished tasks in the same repository. Each task is evaluated in matched uninterrupted and switched sessions, requiring agents to recover task-specific requirements and partial progress while avoiding cross-task confusion. The benchmark provides 200 focus tasks from 19 Python repositories, 400 matched session specifications, and executable verifiers. Across seven coding agents, task switching reduces focus-task resolution by 11.5 percentage points on average. A plug-in context-management module that selects relevant history and maintains task-state summaries improves completion by 5.5–15.5 percentage points on OpenCode. 🌐 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02017 🔥 Project Page: https://mqleet.github.io/Switch-Swe/ 🕹️ Code: https://github.com/Miraclecsc/Switch-SWE

title: Can AI Reviewers See Your Efforts to Improve Your Paper? A Large-Scale Study of Paper Revision Trajectories

details.title: Can AI Reviewers See Your Efforts to Improve Your Paper? A Large-Scale Study of Paper Revision Trajectories
details.abstract: Do AI reviewers recognize the improvements authors make through revision? We introduce PaperTrajectory-2026, covering 6,959 paper trajectories across five AI conferences, with automatic annotations along 14 revision dimensions. Evaluating eight AI reviewers, we find that most revisions annotated as major improvements receive unchanged scores, with weak agreement across reviewers on the direction of score changes. Even when revisions earn higher scores, a brief negative user opinion can erase or reverse that advantage. Our study highlights the need for AI reviewers whose judgments track substantive improvements and remain stable when the scientific evidence is unchanged.

title: You don't need long context

details.title: You don't need long context
details.abstract: Later tokens are costlier to generate than earlier tokens. On frontier open weight models, the disparity in cost may rise to as much as 7x. Through frequent compaction, we show across a broad range of long-horizon and long-input tasks that frontier language models sacrifice little to no task accuracy when maintaining short contexts. We further demonstrate that LLM performance does not collapse on long-horizon software engineering tasks even when taking at most one action per context, and based on that we outline the concept of semantic state space models (SSSMs). Our findings question the need for long-context language models.

title: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena

details.title: Are Frontier VLM Agents Ready to Be Robot Generalists? An Empirical Study with the Embodied Agent Arena
details.abstract: Embodied Agent Arena evaluates ten frontier VLM agents on 1,000 cases across Geometry, Spatial Reasoning, Affordance, Task Planning, and Manipulation. It combines 32 established sources with GeoProbe, a new 168-case benchmark for camera, motion, depth, and scale estimation. The results reveal distinct strengths across models: similar spatial scores can accompany very different planning success, and achieving early subgoals does not ensure completion of a full task sequence. Matched execution traces show where object control, action grounding, and recovery break down. The accompanying video compares all ten models across the five capability domains.

title: Is Your Long-Horizon Benchmark Really Deep? Measuring and Synthesizing Depth in Terminal Tasks

details.title: Is Your Long-Horizon Benchmark Really Deep? Measuring and Synthesizing Depth in Terminal Tasks
details.abstract: Long-horizon terminal tasks are used to evaluate and train agents. Human-curated datasets are scarce, so many synthesis methods have emerged. They usually measure the length of a task by the turns a model needs to pass it, and its difficulty by labels the LLM sets during generation. We find, however, that the turn count largely reflects the habits of the model, not only the demands of the task, and that the labels barely track how often models pass. We describe a terminal task by its work, the number of operations it requires, and its depth, the number of turns that must happen in sequence because the commands of each turn can only be chosen after reading the output of the previous one. Estimating depth as the smallest turn cap, stated to the agent, under which the task passes, we audit 734 tasks from six existing datasets. Synthesis has mostly added work, not depth: 94% of the solved synthetic tasks pass within three turns, yet depth, unlike the turn count, predicts difficulty beyond work. We propose DEPTH, in which a generation agent writes each task one segment at a time in a real software environment, carrying out each segment before writing it and starting the next from the state it leaves. Our 105 tasks exceed every audited dataset in depth and work, and none of six current models passes half of them. Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on runs from these tasks improves it on two terminal benchmarks.

title: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning

details.title: What We Keep of What We Forget: Replacement Operators and Routing Semantics in Training-Free MoE Expert Pruning
details.abstract: The paper provides a controlled fixed-pruning-mask comparison of replacement/rerouting strategies and shows that post-pruning gate scale is part of the pruning algorithm, proposing the trained-scale rule: preserving the router’s training-time normalization convention generally performs best. It introduces the tilted novice, a low-rank input-dependent replacement for pruned experts, which improves over MoNE’s constant replacement with only ~1.2–1.8% additional parameters, while showing that no single replacement operator universally dominates.

title: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models

details.title: Is Forgetting Unified? Exploring Concept Unlearning in Unified Multimodal Models
details.abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks require agents to learn, reason, and generalize robustly across complex real-world environments. However, existing approaches often struggle with partial observability, fragmented spatial reasoning, and inefficient integration of heterogeneous memories, limiting their capacity for long-horizon adaptation. To address this, we introduce RoboMemory, a brain-inspired framework that unifies Temporal, Spatial, Semantic, and Episodic memory for efficient long-horizon planning and interactive learning. Its core innovations are a comprehensive memory system designed for embodied tasks, and a dynamic spatial knowledge graph for scalable, consistent memory updates. Extensive experiments on EmbodiedBench show that RoboMemory improves the average success rate of Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Ins by 26.5 percentage points and achieves performance comparable to strong closed-source VLM agents. Real-world trials further suggest RoboMemory's potential for interactive environmental learning by reusing accumulated experience across repeated task attempts. These results demonstrate RoboMemory as a scalable memory-augmented framework for embodied agents, improving long-horizon planning and cumulative learning in complex interactive environments.

title: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents

details.title: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents
details.abstract: Trajectory-level GRPO is a common approach for training multi-step GUI agents, but repeatedly rolling out complete trajectories from the task root can be inefficient: task-level rewards provide coarse supervision over which intermediate decisions require improvement, while already-mastered prefixes are repeatedly re-executed before reaching difficult states. We introduce a two-stage adaptive training framework that jointly addresses where to learn and how far to roll out. We first construct reusable intermediate checkpoints from successful expert trajectories and select informative pivots using action disagreement, which measures uncertainty directly from sampled GUI actions. Stage I performs one-step RL at these pivots to improve uncertain local decisions. Stage II then progressively expands policy responsibility through adaptive Local, Suffix, and Root training according to task progress. Recoverable checkpoints enable repeated training from intermediate states without replaying the preceding trajectory. Across MobileGym and CUA-Gym-Hub, our method reduces environment interaction by 56-61% relative to Vanilla GRPO while improving task performance, demonstrating that jointly allocating training across states and rollout ranges can substantially improve GUI-agent RL efficiency.

title: SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion via Selective Modeling

details.title: SeMo3D: Unifying 3D Generation, Editing, and Completion via Selective Modeling
details.abstract: 3D generation, editing, and completion are typically treated as regenerating the complete 3D asset under task-specific constraints, even when only a local region needs modification. This leads to task isolation, inconsistency in content that should remain unchanged, and dependence on task-specific paired data. We address these issues with a key observation: the three tasks all synthesize a designated region while keeping the rest intact---the full region for generation, the target region for editing, and the missing region for completion. We term this paradigm Selective Modeling and build SeMo3D upon it; it naturally unifies the three tasks, preserves unchanged content by construction, and enables training without paired editing or completion data, since any 3D asset can be partitioned into a selected region and its context. For training, we propose region-selective denoising, which randomly selects regions of varying sizes on standard 3D assets and applies noise and loss only to them, jointly learning all three tasks. For architecture, we propose Omni3DiT, a multi-condition 3D diffusion transformer that distinguishes regions to create from those to retain and fuses image, text, and point guidance for fine-grained control. Experiments across three benchmarks show SeMo3D surpasses state-of-the-art methods on all tasks, delivering multimodal controllability in generation and strong consistency and accuracy in editing and completion. SeMo3D further serves as a unified modeling tool for agents, enabling efficient 3D creation through natural-language interaction. Project page: https://xiaokunsun.github.io/SeMo3D.github.io Code: https://github.com/XiaokunSun/SeMo3D

title: Muon Makes the First Mixture-of-Experts Layer Harder to Balance

details.title: Muon Makes the First Mixture-of-Experts Layer Harder to Balance
details.abstract: Open MoE recipes disagree on whether Muon should train the router. DeepSeek trains it with Muon, Qwen keeps it on AdamW. We found the router's optimizer isn't the problem. With Muon on the rest of the network, the inputs to the router of the first MoE layer share a direction, and right after warmup its busiest expert gets 4-7x its fair share, vs 1.1x under AdamW. Moving only the router to AdamW makes it worse. Subtracting the batch mean from the router's inputs removes the overload and barely changes the loss. Code and all 145 runs are public.

title: GigaSpeech 3: Scaling Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition with Weakly Labeled Data

details.title: GigaSpeech 3: Scaling Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition with Weakly Labeled Data
details.abstract: 🎙️ GigaSpeech 3 Scaling Multi-Dialect Arabic Speech Recognition with Weakly Labeled Data GigaSpeech 3 is a large-scale, weakly labeled Arabic speech corpus containing approximately 10 million speech segments across Algerian (DZA), Egyptian (EGY), Iraqi (IRQ), Saudi (SAU), and Syrian (SYR) Arabic . It supports dialect-specific and multi-dialect automatic speech recognition (ASR), weak supervision, and low-resource speech research. The accompanying manuscript reports approximately 39,000 hours for its study corpus. Starting from only 51–63 hours of manual transcription per dialect, GigaSpeech 3 combines ASR-biased self-supervised learning, automatic transcription, data selection, and noisy-student refinement to build reusable audio–text supervision. 📥 Download and Demo 📄 Paper: arXiv · PDF 🤗 Training data: GigaSpeech 3 on Hugging Face 🎧 Online demo: Try GigaSpeech 3 Arabic ASR 🧪 Evaluation data: GigaSpeechBench on Hugging Face 🏆 Evaluation toolkit and leaderboard: SpeechColab/GigaSpeechBench See the dataset card for file descriptions and terms of use. The current GitHub repository provides the project overview; training recipes and model checkpoint links will be added as they become available. 🌍 Dataset 🗣️ Dialects Code Dialect DZA Algerian Arabic EGY Egyptian Arabic IRQ Iraqi Arabic SAU Saudi Arabic SYR Syrian Arabic Each dialect is released as a weakly labeled training partition. The manual seed data and MSA data used in the manuscript are separate from these five partitions. Evaluation uses independently transcribed data from GigaSpeechBench and external Arabic corpora.

title: Auto-Research Agent on MSA Organization to Improve Protein-Protein Complex Structure Prediction

details.title: Auto-Research Agent on MSA Organization to Improve Protein-Protein Complex Structure Prediction
details.abstract: Can an autonomous research agent improve AlphaFold 3 without modifying its model weights? We introduce an agent that treats AlphaFold 3 as a black-box experimental instrument, autonomously analyzing and reorganizing MSAs through biological reasoning and iterative, confidence-guided experimentation. Evaluated on 1,015 protein–protein interfaces across three benchmarks, our approach consistently improves prediction accuracy over standard AF3 pipelines while using 60% fewer MSA sequences on average . Our findings highlight the potential of autonomous test-time research for improving scientific foundation models without retraining. We welcome feedback and discussion!
